title: Quantized operator ABI drift causing intermittent crashes and subtle accuracy shifts
creator: Priya Shah
summary: A mismatch between a newly deployed quantized operator library and the runtime ABI produced intermittent crash loops on several dedicated fleets and produced subtle accuracy drift for some quantized models. This postmortem summarizes detection, impact, root cause, immediate mitigations, and long-term action items to prevent recurrence.
incident_timeline: 2026-02-24 02:13 UTC: Automated rollout of quant-ops-lib v2.7 started to 20% of Dedicated shard pool (canary).
2026-02-24 02:29 UTC: Canary telemetry showed increased 5xx rate on canary hosts; alerts routed to on-call SRE and quant-runtime owners.
2026-02-24 02:45 UTC: Crash rate spiked on canary hosts; automated canary rollback failed due to mixed ABI handling in the serving node process (in-process operator load path).
2026-02-24 03:05 UTC: We paused rollout and promoted emergency mitigation: set routing to bypass canary hosts and force float fallback for affected tenants.

2026-02-24 04:20 UTC: Investigation revealed a silent operator ABI change where a kernel dispatch signature changed ordering of auxiliary flags; some models began producing token-probability deviations without full crashes.

2026-02-24 08:40 UTC: Rollback of quant-ops-lib to v2.6 completed; crash loops subsided but accuracy drift remained visible for a subset of in-flight cached responses until KV caches were invalidated.

2026-02-24 12:00 UTC: Full mitigation: disable new autotuner profiles and re-run targeted eval suite against affected model + workload combinations; create short-term alert for top-100 model fidelity metrics.
2026-02-25 09:00 UTC: Root cause analysis completed and action items assigned.
root_cause: An operator library release (quant-ops-lib v2.7) inadvertently changed an internal kernel dispatch ABI: the optional-aux flags field was reordered when a new backend optimization was enabled. The serving runtime assumed stable dispatch ordering and did not validate operator fingerprints at load time. When the runtime dynamically bound op implementations across mixed-version shared objects, some kernels executed with mismatched parameter ordering, causing nondeterministic numeric differences (accuracy drift) and, in a smaller set of codepaths, memory-safety issues that produced crash loops.
impact: Incidents affected 12 Dedicated clusters and 6% of hosted inference requests for customers using the new quant profiles during the rollout window. Observed effects: transient crash loops causing 5xx-rate increase from 0.02% baseline to 2.1% on canary shards, and soft correctness regressions (per-token probability drift) impacting end-to-end eval pass-rates by up to 7 percentage points for three production models. Two enterprise customers experienced degraded SLAs and opened support tickets.
detection: The issue was detected by automated canary dashboards (5xx spike) and later corroborated by daily fidelity evals that flagged a regression in the model-specific prompt suite. SRE pager escalations and on-call devs performed the first mitigation steps. Post-incident, additional signal from token-level delta histograms helped quantify the scope of accuracy drift.
mitigation_taken: Paused rollout and routed new traffic away from canary hosts
Forced float-path fallback for affected requests to avoid using the quantized kernel set
Rolled back quant-ops-lib to v2.6 across all fleets
Invalidated KV/prefix caches where cached quantized outputs could include drifted token sequences
Disabled autotuner profiles that produced the new operator variant until compatibility tests passed
Added short-term alerting on per-model fidelity deltas for top-customer models
action_items: Operator ABI and fingerprinting: Add a strict operator fingerprinting check at runtime load time that includes dispatch signature, flag ordering, and backend capability bitmask. Fail fast if mismatch detected. (Owner: runtime-kernel, ETA: 2 weeks)

Canary hardening: Extend canary gating to validate per-model fidelity suites (golden prompts) before promoting operator libs beyond 10% traffic. Integrate automated eval pass/fail as a gate. (Owner: infra-qa, ETA: 3 weeks)

Binary compatibility checklist: Require a signed compatibility matrix for every quant-ops-lib build declaring ABI-preserving changes; block auto-rollouts if matrix absent. (Owner: release-engineering, ETA: 1 week)

Autotuner safeguards: Instrument autotuner to produce deterministic operator variants and to publish 'compatibility tags' with each generated profile; disallow untagged profiles in production. (Owner: quant-autotuner, ETA: 4 weeks)

Runtime sandboxing: Add lightweight isolated operator load mode on canaries that triggers full process restart upon operator mismatch instead of attempting mixed in-process binding. (Owner: serving-runtime, ETA: 6 weeks)
Observability improvements: Surface token-level delta histograms and per-model KL divergence on Console with alerting for deviations > 3 sigma. (Owner: console-observability, ETA: 3 weeks)
Regression tests: Add fuzz tests that mix operator versions and flags and assert numeric equivalence within defined tolerances; include as pre-merge checks. (Owner: infra-qa, ETA: 2 weeks)

Customer communication: Draft post-incident customer communication summarizing root cause and assurances; offer targeted assistance to affected enterprise tenants. (Owner: support & comms, ETA: 3 business days)
Release gating: Introduce a release block that prevents operator library rollouts that change dispatch ordering without explicit approval. (Owner: release-engineering, ETA: 2 weeks)
KV cache hygiene: Ensure cache invalidation is part of operator rollout playbook when deploying quant operator changes. (Owner: serving-runtime, ETA: 1 week)

Legacy compatibility layer: Plan for a short-lived compatibility adapter library that normalizes dispatch signatures across minor versions to give time for rolling upgrades. (Owner: runtime-kernel, ETA: 8 weeks, follow-up required)
Audit and retro: Conduct a cross-team tabletop to review why rollout automation didn't stop the deployment despite failing canary signals; update runbooks accordingly. (Owner: SRE, ETA: 1 week)
follow_up_notes: We observed that older models with fused attention kernels were more sensitive to the dispatch ordering change; prioritize those models for early re-eval after fixes.
Engineering decision: prefer fail-fast on ABI mismatch rather than attempting mixed-version operator binding; this reduces risk of silent correctness regressions.
Plan to schedule a dedicated week (Quant Reliability Week) to close the top 6 action items and validate fixes against the customer-facing eval corpus.
Consider adding a per-customer 'compatibility profile' flag so customers can opt into aggressive autotuner profiles with explicit acceptance of potential minor fidelity variance.
